We develop a 10 m Sentinel-2 convolutional model for mapping canopy mortality across six forest landscapes spanning humid, temperate, and seasonally dry conditions. Labels were digitized from field-verified polygons, and the intended use is prediction in forest landscapes not used during model fitting.

The 120,000 labelled pixels were randomly divided 80:20 into training and test sets. Pixels from the same field polygons and adjacent image neighbourhoods could therefore occur in both sets; hyperparameters were selected with additional random pixel folds. The resulting test AUC was 0.94.

Because the test score is high across the pooled sample, we conclude that the model generalizes reliably to unseen forest landscapes across the study region.

We estimate monthly lake-surface chlorophyll from atmospherically corrected multispectral imagery for 14 lakes over three years. The product is intended for routine seasonal monitoring, including periods with haze and partial cloud cover.

Validation retained only pixels carrying the highest retrieval-quality flag and removed all scenes with more than 10% cloud cover. An optical satellite record is used to estimate seasonal surface albedo over Arctic sea ice. Daily grid cells without valid retrievals are filled by linear interpolation before calculating monthly means.
